points.title: 贫困童年
points.description: 法拉第出生于伦敦一个贫困的铁匠家庭，是家中四个孩子中的第三个。由于家境困难，他只接受了基本的读写教育，12岁时便辍学成为书籍装订学徒。这段经历使他接触到了大量科学书籍，激发了他对科学的浓厚兴趣。他利用装订间隙阅读《大英百科全书》等科学著作，并开始参加市哲学会的讲座，为日后科学事业奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Faraday was born into a poor blacksmith's family in London, the third of four children. Due to financial hardship, he received only basic education and left school at age 12 to become an apprentice bookbinder. This job exposed him to numerous scientific books, sparking his profound interest in science. He used his spare time to read scientific works like the Encyclopaedia Britannica and began attending lectures at the City Philosophical Society, laying the foundation for his future scientific career.

points.title: 科学启蒙
points.description: 1812年，法拉第作为著名化学家戴维的听众参加了四次讲座，并整理了详细的笔记。他将这些笔记精心装订后送给戴维， impressed戴维并获得了实验室助理的职位。1813年，他随戴维前往欧洲大陆进行为期18个月的科学考察，访问了法国、意大利等国的科学中心，接触了当时欧洲最前沿的科学思想和实验技术，极大地扩展了他的科学视野。
points.descriptionEn: In 1812, Faraday attended four lectures by renowned chemist Humphry Davy and meticulously documented them in notes. He presented these bound notes to Davy, who was impressed and offered him a position as laboratory assistant. In 1813, Faraday accompanied Davy on an 18-month scientific tour of continental Europe, visiting scientific centers in France, Italy and other countries, exposing him to cutting-edge European scientific ideas and experimental techniques, significantly broadening his scientific horizons.

points.title: 化学研究
points.description: 在皇家研究所期间，法拉第开始了独立的化学研究工作。他发现了苯，研究了氯的液化，发明了本生灯的前身，并系统研究了电解现象。1825年，他被任命为皇家研究所实验室主任，1833年成为化学教授。这一时期，他发表了大量化学论文，在有机化学和电化学领域做出了重要贡献，奠定了他在科学界的地位。同时，他定期举办面向公众的科学讲座，普及科学知识。
points.descriptionEn: During his time at the Royal Institution, Faraday began independent chemical research. He discovered benzene, studied the liquefaction of chlorine, invented a precursor to the Bunsen burner, and systematically investigated electrolysis. In 1825, he was appointed Director of the Royal Institution's Laboratory, and in 1833 became Professor of Chemistry. During this period, he published numerous chemical papers, making significant contributions to organic and electrochemistry, establishing his reputation in the scientific community. He also regularly delivered public lectures to popularize science.

points.title: 电磁学突破
points.description: 1831年是法拉第科学生涯的转折点，他发现了电磁感应现象，证明了电和磁之间的联系。通过实验，他发现当磁铁穿过线圈时会产生电流，这一发现奠定了电磁学的基础，为后来的发电机、变压器等电力设备提供了理论基础。随后，他提出了电力线、磁场等概念，发展了电磁场理论。这些工作不仅改变了物理学的发展方向，也为现代电力工业和通信技术奠定了基础。1851年，他发现法拉第效应，证明了光的电磁性质。
points.descriptionEn: 1831 marked a turning point in Faraday's scientific career when he discovered electromagnetic induction, demonstrating the connection between electricity and magnetism. Through experiments, he found that moving a magnet through a wire coil generates electric current, a discovery that laid the foundation for electromagnetism and provided the theoretical basis for later generators, transformers and other electrical devices. Subsequently, he introduced concepts like electric field lines and magnetic fields, developing the theory of electromagnetic fields. These works not only changed the direction of physics but also laid the foundation for modern electric power industry and communication technology. In 1851, he discovered the Faraday effect, proving the electromagnetic nature of light.

points.title: 晚年生活
points.description: 1855年后，法拉第的健康状况逐渐恶化，记忆力衰退，但他仍坚持科学思考和写作。他拒绝了维多利亚女王授予的爵位，一生保持简朴生活。1867年，他在汉普斯特德的家中去世，享年75岁。法拉第一生发表了大量科学论文，著有《电学实验研究》等著作。他不仅是一位杰出的科学家，还是一位优秀的科普工作者，他的科学讲座深受欢迎，对后世科学教育和普及产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: After 1855, Faraday's health gradually declined with memory loss, but he continued scientific thinking and writing. He refused a knighthood from Queen Victoria, maintaining a simple lifestyle throughout his life. In 1867, he died at his home in Hampstead at age 75. Faraday published numerous scientific papers and authored works such as 'Experimental Researches in Electricity'. He was not only an outstanding scientist but also an excellent science communicator, whose popular lectures were widely received and had a profound impact on later science education and popularization.

appraisal.zh: 法拉第被公认为19世纪最伟大的物理学家和化学家之一，其电磁感应理论改变了人类对电与磁的理解，为现代电力工业奠定基础；他出身贫寒、自学成才，并以面向公众的科学讲座推动科学普及，其强调实验观察的理念至今影响科学研究与科学教育。也有研究者指出，他数学能力有限，理论缺乏严格的数学表达，场论思想当时多受质疑与忽视，晚年对光的波动说持保留态度，未能完全接受麦克斯韦的统一理论，其宗教信念有时也被认为影响了科学判断。总体而言，他被视为实验物理学的奠基人之一，其名字与肖像成为科学精神的象征。
appraisal.en: Faraday is recognized as one of the greatest physicists and chemists of the 19th century: his theory of electromagnetic induction transformed understanding of electricity and magnetism and laid the foundation of the modern electric power industry, and his rise from poverty through self-education and his public lectures made science accessible beyond the elite, while his emphasis on experimental observation still shapes research and science education. Yet some researchers note his limited mathematical ability and the lack of rigorous mathematical expression in his theories, the contemporary skepticism toward his field ideas, his later reservations about the wave theory of light and failure to fully accept Maxwell's unified theory, and the occasional influence of his religious beliefs on his scientific judgment. Overall, he is regarded as a founder of experimental physics, his name and portrait symbols of the scientific spirit.

supporter.zh: 法拉第被视为19世纪最伟大的物理学家和化学家之一，他的电磁感应理论彻底改变了人类对电和磁的理解，为现代电力工业奠定了基础。他出身贫寒却通过自学成为科学巨匠，体现了科学民主化的精神。作为科普先驱，他面向公众的科学讲座使科学知识不再局限于精英阶层，对科学普及做出了不可磨灭的贡献。他的实验方法和科学思维至今仍影响着科学研究的方式。
supporter.en: Faraday is regarded as one of the greatest physicists and chemists of the 19th century, whose electromagnetic induction theory revolutionized human understanding of electricity and magnetism, laying the foundation for modern electric power industry. Rising from humble beginnings to become a scientific giant through self-education, he embodied the spirit of scientific democratization. As a pioneer of science popularization, his public lectures made scientific knowledge accessible beyond the elite, making an indelible contribution to science communication. His experimental methods and scientific thinking continue to influence the way scientific research is conducted today.

critic.zh: 批评者指出法拉第的数学能力有限，他的理论缺乏严格的数学表达，这在一定程度上限制了他理论的传播和发展。他的场论思想在当时也受到许多物理学家的质疑和忽视。此外，法拉第在晚年对光的波动说持保留态度，未能完全接受麦克斯韦的电磁理论统一。他的宗教信仰有时被认为影响了他的科学判断，特别是在某些科学问题上倾向于神秘主义解释。
critic.en: Critics point out that Faraday had limited mathematical abilities, and his theories lacked rigorous mathematical expression, which to some extent limited the dissemination and development of his work. His field theory ideas were also questioned and ignored by many physicists at the time. Additionally, Faraday remained skeptical about the wave theory of light in his later years and failed to fully accept Maxwell's unified electromagnetic theory. His religious beliefs are sometimes thought to have influenced his scientific judgments, particularly his tendency toward mystical explanations in certain scientific matters.

objective.zh: 在历史学界，法拉第被公认为实验物理学的奠基人之一，他的工作标志着物理学从牛顿力学向现代物理学的转变。在流行文化中，法拉第常被描绘为出身卑微却通过勤奋和才华改变命运的励志典范。他的名字被用于命名电容单位'法拉'，他的肖像出现在英国20英镑纸币上，成为科学精神的象征。法拉第的科学遗产不仅体现在他的具体发现上，更体现在他强调实验观察和科学普及的理念，这些理念至今仍影响着科学教育和公众理解科学的方式。
objective.en: In historical scholarship, Faraday is recognized as one of the founders of experimental physics, and his work marked the transition of physics from Newtonian mechanics to modern physics. In popular culture, Faraday is often portrayed as an inspirational figure who rose from humble circumstances to change his destiny through diligence and talent. His name is commemorated in the unit of capacitance, the farad, and his portrait appears on the British £20 banknote, symbolizing the spirit of science. Faraday's scientific legacy is not only reflected in his specific discoveries but also in his emphasis on experimental observation and science popularization—ideas that continue to influence science education and public understanding of science today.
